answer: Draw the economy as an atlas of who works with whom. An identity's weight is the number of separate paths, sharing no bridge, that link it to the established core. A farm is an island: a thousand puppets trade among themselves, but every path out crosses the same one or two bridges, so its whole weight is capped at what those bridges carry, however many names it mints. Lifting the cap means building many sustained crossings with strangers who owe the farm nothing. Under sable scrutiny each new bridge must be real work, real counterparty, so influence costs relationships, not keys.
